description: Get product filter limits and supported presentation choices. max_per_store includes built-in and disabled filters. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for GET /api/2025-01/product-filters/contract. Only the connected store is accessible.

description: List attributes and metafield definitions available as filter sources. Each source includes compatible filter types, display choices, and a recommended configuration. Sources already used by a filter are omitted. A metafield definition must be readable by the token, visible on the storefront, and enabled for filtering. metafield_owner_type distinguishes product and variant definitions. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for GET /api/2025-01/product-filters/sources. Only the connected store is accessible.

limit.description: Number of sources, from 1 to source_list_max. Omission uses source_list_default; an oversized limit is rejected.

offset.description: Number of matching sources to skip.

search.description: Match a source by its name, namespace, key, or slug.

source_type.description: Source family to list: attribute or metafield.

description: Search, filter, and sort the store's storefront product filters. The top-level revision covers the complete list; use it when reordering. Each definition has its own revision for updates. source_available reflects whether its source remains eligible and readable by the token. Sorting this response does not change storefront order. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for GET /api/2025-01/product-filters. Only the connected store is accessible.

search.description: Match label or filter_key.

sort_by.description: One of the contract's sort_columns.

source_type.description: Filter by system, attribute, or metafield.

name: list_product_filters

description: Create a storefront filter from an attribute or metafield definition. Choose a filter type and display type supported by the source. The service derives filter_key: for example, the Material attribute yields `attribute:material`, while a product metafield with namespace specs and key material yields `metafield:product:specs.material`. enabled defaults to true. allow_multiple defaults to true for multi_enum and color, and false for other filter types; range filters cannot allow multiple values. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for POST /api/2025-01/product-filters. Only the connected store is accessible. Preserve omitted fields. Present confirmation impact before resubmitting with confirmation; inspect bulk success and failure results. Do not retry an uncertain write automatically.

allow_multiple.description: Whether shoppers may select more than one choice. Use the source recommendation; ranges require false.

display_type.description: Storefront control supported by the selected source and filter type.

enabled.description: Whether the filter is enabled immediately. Defaults to true when omitted.

filter_type.description: Filter behavior supported by the selected source.

label.description: Shopper-facing label in the store's default language.

sort_order.description: Initial storefront position from zero through sort_order_max. Omit to append after the current filters.

source_id.description: Attribute id or Metafield Definition id returned by List product filter sources.

description: Replace the complete storefront filter order atomically. Read the unfiltered list, then send its top-level revision and every definition id once, including disabled filters. Reordering also changes each definition revision, so read the list again before a later update. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for PUT /api/2025-01/product-filters/reorder. Only the connected store is accessible. Preserve omitted fields. definition_ids.description: Every current definition id in the desired order. Replace these example IDs with the full unfiltered list from your store.

revision.description: Complete-list revision from an unfiltered List product filters response.

Changing a base-language label marks its translations outdated without deleting them. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for PUT /api/2025-01/product-filters/{id}. sort_order.description: Storefront position, from zero through the contract's sort_order_max. Prefer the atomic reorder endpoint for list reordering.

idempotency_key.description: Optional stable key for this translation write. Reuse only for the exact same intended request.

translations.description: Field-keyed string values. Only label is supported.

Every requested filter must belong to the token's store. Fields without a translation in this locale are omitted from the response. An omitted field is not empty: shoppers see the store's base-language value, which the resource's own GET endpoint returns. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for GET /api/2025-01/product-filters/translations/{locale}. Only the connected store is accessible.
name: get_product_filter_translations

description: Update several filter labels atomically. Each row contains a filter UUID and fields with label. The entire request succeeds or fails together. allow_anonymous.description: Accept reviews from guests who are not signed in. Guests must enter a name. Invited customers can always review what they bought. Default false.

auto_approve_guest_reviews.description: Let guest reviews follow moderation_mode like customers' reviews. While false, every guest review is pending until approved. Default false.

block_emails.description: Refuse submissions whose title, text or reviewer name contains an email address, with STORE_REVIEW_EMAILS_NOT_ALLOWED. Default true.

block_urls.description: Refuse submissions whose title, text or reviewer name contains a web address, with STORE_REVIEW_LINKS_NOT_ALLOWED. Default true.

blocked_words.description: Complete blocked word list. A submission containing any of these words or phrases, in its title, text or reviewer name, is refused with STORE_REVIEW_BLOCKED_WORDS. Default [].

enable_responses.description: Allow public store responses to reviews. Default true.

flag_low_ratings.description: In auto_approve mode, keep 1- and 2-star reviews pending until they are approved. Has no effect in manual mode, where every review is pending. Default false.

max_content_length.description: Maximum review text length, in characters. Default 1000.

max_images.description: Maximum photos per review, from 1 through max_images_max. Default 3.

min_content_length.description: Minimum review text length, in characters. Default 20.

moderation_mode.description: auto_approve publishes each review that passes the content filters as soon as it is submitted, unless flag_low_ratings holds it for approval; manual keeps every review pending until it is approved; disabled stops new reviews and helpful votes and hides existing reviews from the storefront. Default auto_approve.

require_purchase.description: Accept reviews only from customers whose order for the product counts as a purchase (paid, cash on delivery, or partly or fully refunded; never cancelled or test orders), or from a review invitation. Cannot be true while allow_anonymous is true. Default false.

review_request_delay_days.description: Days after an order is fully delivered before the review request is sent (0-60). Default 3.

reviewer_display.description: How reviewer names appear on the storefront: anonymous, first_name, full_name, or initials. Default first_name.

description: List store products. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for GET /api/2025-01/products. Only the connected store is accessible.

brand_ids.description: Comma-separated brand IDs; matches any listed brand.

category_ids.description: Comma-separated category IDs; matches products in any listed category.

collection_id.description: Filter by collection membership. Collections are rule-based, so membership follows each collection's rules.

collection_ids.description: Comma-separated collection UUIDs; matches membership in any listed collection.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous `products.list` response. Omit for the first page; reset when search, filters, or sorting changes.

gift_only.description: Set `true` to return only gift-only products or `false` to exclude gift-only products. Omit to include both.

ids.description: Comma-separated product IDs, up to `list_max_limit`; returns only those products. Use it to fetch a known set in one call instead of one call per product. IDs that do not exist are left out.

include_total.description: Set to false to omit `total` from a filtered first page. Pages read with `cursor` never include a filtered `total`. Unfiltered lists always include `total`.

is_gift_card.description: Filter Gift Card products. Omit to include both ordinary and Gift Card products; gift_only is a different, free-gift classification.

limit.description: Page size from 1 to `list_max_limit`. Omit to use `list_default_limit` from Product limits. Values above the maximum are rejected.

location_id.description: Filter to products with inventory at this location.

location_ids.description: Comma-separated location UUIDs; matches inventory at any listed location.

low_stock_only.description: Return products at or below a configured low-stock threshold.

price_max.description: Maximum regular price in the store currency.

price_min.description: Minimum regular price in the store currency.

search.description: Search text; surrounding whitespace is removed. Text exceeding `search_max_length` is rejected.

search_field.description: Defaults to `all`: matches product titles, product/variant SKUs and barcodes, tags, and full-text matches in titles, descriptions, vendor names and brand names. Choose `title`, `sku`, `barcode`, `vendor`, `brand`, `tag`, or `variant_sku` to narrow the search. `sku` searches product SKUs; `variant_sku` searches variant SKUs. `barcode` searches both product and variant barcodes.

sort_by.description: A value from `sort_columns` in Product limits. Defaults to `created_at`. Price sorts use the store currency; variable products sort by their minimum variant price. Equal values use ascending product ID as a tie-breaker; missing values sort last.

status.description: Filter: active, scheduled, draft, or archived.

stock_max.description: Maximum displayed available stock. Untracked products do not match.

stock_min.description: Minimum displayed available stock. Untracked products do not match.

tag_id.description: Filter by assigned tag ID. A tag that does not exist or is being deleted matches no products.

tag_ids.description: Comma-separated assigned tag IDs. Use `tag_match` to choose whether any or all IDs must match. A tag that does not exist or is being deleted is rejected.

vendor_ids.description: Comma-separated vendor IDs; matches any listed vendor.

limit.description: Positive page size. Omit to use `variant_list_page_size` from Product limits. Values above `variant_list_max_limit` are capped; the response reports the effective size as `per_page`.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Omit to use page 1.

name: list_product_variants

description: List the store's variants changed since a time. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for GET /api/2025-01/variants. Only the connected store is accessible.

cursor.description: Opaque `next_cursor` from the previous page. Send the same `updated_since` with it.

limit.description: Positive page size. Omit to use `variant_list_page_size` from Product limits. Values above `variant_list_max_limit` are capped; the response reports the effective size as `per_page`.

updated_since.description: RFC 3339 timestamp. Only variants whose `updated_at` is at or after it are listed. Omit for every variant.

description: Fetch one variant by id. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for GET /api/2025-01/products/{id}/variants/{variantId}. Only the connected store is accessible.
name: get_product_variant

description: Create a product. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for POST /api/2025-01/products. Only the connected store is accessible. Preserve omitted fields. Present confirmation impact before resubmitting with confirmation; inspect bulk success and failure results. Do not retry an uncertain write automatically.

attribute_ids.description: Attribute IDs that define the variant combinations. Required for variable products. Each variant must provide one value per declared attribute. On update, replaces the declaration, subject to the surviving variants and store limits. Variable products only.

barcode.description: Optional Barcode/GTIN for a simple product; variable products use variant barcodes. ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens are accepted. Must be unique across products and variants. See barcode_max_length. Simple products only.

brand_id.description: Brand ID in this store. On create, omit if unassigned. On update, omit or send null to keep the assignment; send 0 to clear it.

category_ids.description: Category IDs in this store, up to max_categories. Duplicates are removed. On update, replaces the assignment set; [] clears it and omission keeps it.

channel_ids.description: Sales-channel IDs in this store. Omission on create leaves the product unassigned. On update, replaces the assignment set; [] clears it and omission keeps it.

condition.description: Merchandise condition. Defaults to new. Variants may override the parent condition. Allowed values: `new`, `used`, `refurbished`.

description.description: Rich HTML description. Unsafe HTML is removed. The sanitized HTML, including markup, must fit description_max_length.

dimension_unit.description: Dimension unit; required when any dimension is supplied. Allowed values: `cm`, `mm`, `m`, `in`, `ft`.

gift_only.description: Defaults to false. When true, direct cart additions are rejected with CART_GIFT_ONLY; the product can be added only as an eligible free gift. This flag does not hide the product from listings.

height.description: Positive package height within the store’s limit.

hide_from_listings.description: Defaults to false. Excludes the product from storefront search and browse listings while keeping its assigned-channel product page accessible by direct link. Does not change gift_only or channel assignments.

hs_code.description: Customs HS code. See hs_code_max_length and the field constraints in GET /products/limits.

images.description: Gallery entries: {file_id, alt_text?, sort_order?}. Files may be images, videos, or 3D models. Non-empty file_id values require read_files. On update, the array replaces the gallery; [] clears it. The store’s max_images limit applies.

inventory.description: Simple products with inventory_source=track. Rows are {location_id, quantity, low_stock_threshold?, expected_quantity?}. Quantities are non-negative integers within the store’s limits. On update, only named locations change. expected_quantity is the on-hand value previously read (0 for a missing row); a mismatch returns 409 PRODUCT_VERSION_STALE. You may use merchant-managed locations or locations owned by your app’s active installation.

inventory_group_id.description: Inventory-group UUID. Required with inventory_source=group. The group must belong to this store. Simple products only.

inventory_source.description: Simple-product inventory mode: track for per-location stock, none for untracked stock, or group for an inventory-group link. Defaults to track. Changing modes on update may require confirmation. Allowed values: `track`, `none`, `group`. Simple products only.

length.description: Positive package length within the store’s limit.

max_order_quantity.description: Optional per-order quantity cap, independent of inventory mode. On update, 0 clears the explicit cap; omission or null leaves it unchanged. Without an explicit cap, the store’s default order cap may still apply.

metafields.description: Values as {definition_id, value}. Definitions must target products and permit your app to write them. On update, this array replaces the set your app can write; [] clears that set. Use the dedicated metafield endpoint for writes addressed by namespace and key.

mpn.description: Optional manufacturer part number. Not required to be unique. See mpn_max_length.

no_manufacturer_identifiers.description: Set true only if the product has no manufacturer identifiers. Cannot be true with a barcode or MPN. The response’s identifier_status is provided when identifiers exist, not_applicable when this flag is true, and unknown otherwise.

overall_low_stock_threshold.description: Overall low-stock threshold for directly tracked simple products. Uses total available stock across locations. Zero is valid. On update, null disables the alert and omission keeps it. Not available for untracked or group-backed stock. Simple products only.

prices.description: Simple products only. Rows are {currency_code, regular_price, sale_price?, cost_price?, sale_starts_at?, sale_ends_at?}. Amounts are JSON decimal strings with the currency’s permitted precision. Include the base currency. On update, supplying this array replaces the complete price set. A sale price may be zero but must be below the regular price. The base-currency sale schedule applies to all currency sale prices; a non-base sale requires a base sale. Omit sale prices from the replacement set to remove them.

publish_at.description: Publication time, required when the resulting status is scheduled. Accepts an ISO 8601 timestamp; include an offset for an explicit instant, or use the store timezone for a local timestamp. Stay within publish_max_days_ahead from GET /products/limits. Invalid local times during a daylight-saving change are rejected; a repeated local time uses its first occurrence. Changing to another status clears the schedule.

requires_shipping.description: Defaults to true and can be changed on update. Variants follow this value unless they set their own requires_shipping. While it is false, the product and every variant that follows it reject weight, dimensions, customs fields, and per-item shipping prices; values stored earlier are kept but not used.

seo_description.description: Search-engine description. Whitespace is trimmed and control characters are rejected. See seo_description_max_length.

seo_title.description: Search-engine title. Whitespace is trimmed and control characters are rejected. See seo_title_max_length.

shipping_prices.description: Simple products only. Per-currency flat shipping overrides: {currency_code, price}. Send price as an exact decimal string using that currency's precision.

short_description.description: Plain-text summary. Surrounding whitespace is removed and control characters are rejected. See short_description_max_length.

sku.description: Required product SKU, including for a variable parent. ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, periods, and slashes are accepted. Trimmed and kept as entered, and unique across products, variants, and inventory groups in the store regardless of letter casing: ABC-1 and abc-1 are the same SKU. See sku_max_length.

slug.description: URL slug. Omit on create to generate it from the title. A source slug must use lowercase, hyphen-separated words and stay within slug_max_length. A duplicate source slug receives a suffix. On update, omit to keep it; changing it creates a redirect unless create_redirect is false.

status.description: Product status: draft, active, scheduled, or archived. Defaults to draft. Scheduled products require publish_at. Active products are available only through their assigned sales channels. Allowed values: `active`, `scheduled`, `draft`, `archived`.

tag_ids.description: Tag IDs in this store, up to max_tags. Duplicates are removed. On update, replaces the assignment set; [] clears it and omission keeps it.

tax_classes.description: Per-market tax assignment: {market_id, tax_class_id}. Supplied array replaces the full set.

template_handle.description: Existing product template handle for this store. Use default_product for the default template. Omit on update to keep the assignment; an empty string is invalid.

title.description: Product title. Required on create; cannot be empty on update. Normalized to NFC. Control characters are rejected. See title_max_length in GET /products/limits.

type.description: Required on create: simple or variable. Cannot be changed after creation. Allowed values: `simple`, `variable`.

variants.description:
Variable products only; required (at least one variant). The initial variant set, validated together: combination uniqueness against the declared attributes, attribute coverage, at least one variant, and store-wide SKU uniqueness. Each entry:

- `sku` (string, required) — unique across the entire store.
- `attribute_values` (array, required) — One entry per declared attribute: `{attribute_id, option_id}`, choosing one of that attribute's options. Attribute and option ids come from `GET /attributes` (the product's `attribute_ids` must cover every `attribute_id` used). Two variants can never share the same combination.
- `prices` (array, required) — per-currency rows `{currency_code, regular_price, sale_price?, cost_price?, sale_starts_at?, sale_ends_at?}`; the base currency row is required. Amounts are decimal strings.
- `title` (string, optional) — auto-composed from option labels ("Red / M") unless supplied.
- `barcode` is variant-specific. `condition`, `mpn`, and `no_manufacturer_identifiers` can override the parent’s values. `identifier_status` describes whether identifiers are provided, unknown, or not applicable; use the identifier fields and declaration consistently.
- `weight`, `weight_unit`, `length`, `width`, `height`, `dimension_unit`, `hs_code`, `country_of_origin` — physical overrides.
- `requires_shipping` (boolean or null, optional) — this variant's own shipping setting, for example a hardcover that ships beside a PDF that does not. Omit it or send null to follow the product. A variant that does not ship cannot have weight, dimensions, customs fields, or `shipping_prices`.
- `inventory_source` (`track` | `none` | `group`), `inventory` (per-location rows `{location_id, quantity, low_stock_threshold?, expected_quantity?}` when tracking), `inventory_group_id` (when `group`).
- `image_file_id` (string, optional) — Media-library upload UUID; non-empty values require `read_files` in addition to `write_products`. `image_id` selects an existing product gallery row and does not require `read_files`.
- `max_order_quantity` is an optional per-order cap; `overall_low_stock_threshold` applies only to directly tracked stock.

vendor_id.description: Vendor ID in this store. On create, omit if unassigned. On update, omit or send null to keep the assignment; send 0 to clear it.

weight.description: Positive weight within the store’s limit. Requires weight_unit.

description: Update selected product fields. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for PUT /api/2025-01/products/{id}. Only the connected store is accessible. Preserve omitted fields. Present confirmation impact before resubmitting with confirmation; inspect bulk success and failure results. Do not retry an uncertain write automatically.

attribute_ids.description: Attribute IDs that define the variant combinations. Required for variable products. Each variant must provide one value per declared attribute. On update, replaces the declaration, subject to the surviving variants and store limits. Variable products only.

barcode.description: Optional Barcode/GTIN for a simple product; variable products use variant barcodes. ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens are accepted. Must be unique across products and variants. See barcode_max_length. Simple products only.

brand_id.description: Brand ID in this store. On create, omit if unassigned. On update, omit or send null to keep the assignment; send 0 to clear it.

catalog_position.description: Merchant-curated position for the storefront featured listing sort. Sparse, NON-unique positive integers — ties order deterministically by product id, gaps are encouraged (10, 20, 30) so products slot between without renumbering. Nil/cleared products trail the positioned set.

category_ids.description: Category IDs in this store, up to max_categories. Duplicates are removed. On update, replaces the assignment set; [] clears it and omission keeps it.

channel_ids.description: Sales-channel IDs in this store. Omission on create leaves the product unassigned. On update, replaces the assignment set; [] clears it and omission keeps it.

condition.description: Merchandise condition. Defaults to new. Variants may override the parent condition. Allowed values: `new`, `used`, `refurbished`.

confirmation_token.description: Token returned with the impact details for this update.

confirmed.description: Set true when repeating a request after CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED.

create_redirect.description: When changing the slug, create a redirect from the old URL. Defaults to true.

description.description: Rich HTML description. Unsafe HTML is removed. The sanitized HTML, including markup, must fit description_max_length.

dimension_unit.description: Dimension unit; required when any dimension is supplied. Allowed values: `cm`, `mm`, `m`, `in`, `ft`.

expected_revision.description: Copy `revision` from Get product. A product changed since that read returns `PRODUCT_VERSION_STALE` instead of overwriting the newer save.

gift_only.description: Defaults to false. When true, direct cart additions are rejected with CART_GIFT_ONLY; the product can be added only as an eligible free gift. This flag does not hide the product from listings.

height.description: Positive package height within the store’s limit.

hide_from_listings.description: Defaults to false. Excludes the product from storefront search and browse listings while keeping its assigned-channel product page accessible by direct link. Does not change gift_only or channel assignments.

hs_code.description: Customs HS code. See hs_code_max_length and the field constraints in GET /products/limits.

images.description: Gallery entries: {file_id, alt_text?, sort_order?}. Files may be images, videos, or 3D models. Non-empty file_id values require read_files. On update, the array replaces the gallery; [] clears it. The store’s max_images limit applies.

inventory.description: Simple products with inventory_source=track. Rows are {location_id, quantity, low_stock_threshold?, expected_quantity?}. Quantities are non-negative integers within the store’s limits. On update, only named locations change. expected_quantity is the on-hand value previously read (0 for a missing row); a mismatch returns 409 PRODUCT_VERSION_STALE. You may use merchant-managed locations or locations owned by your app’s active installation.

inventory_group_id.description: Inventory-group UUID. Required with inventory_source=group. The group must belong to this store. Simple products only.

inventory_source.description: Simple-product inventory mode: track for per-location stock, none for untracked stock, or group for an inventory-group link. Defaults to track. Changing modes on update may require confirmation. Allowed values: `track`, `none`, `group`. Simple products only.

length.description: Positive package length within the store’s limit.

max_order_quantity.description: Optional per-order quantity cap, independent of inventory mode. On update, 0 clears the explicit cap; omission or null leaves it unchanged. Without an explicit cap, the store’s default order cap may still apply.

metafields.description: Values as {definition_id, value}. Definitions must target products and permit your app to write them. On update, this array replaces the set your app can write; [] clears that set. Use the dedicated metafield endpoint for writes addressed by namespace and key.

mpn.description: Optional manufacturer part number. Not required to be unique. See mpn_max_length.

new_variants.description: Variable products only. Brand-new variants to add alongside the existing set — same entry shape as create's variants array. Combination uniqueness is validated against the surviving existing variants and within the batch.

no_manufacturer_identifiers.description: Set true only if the product has no manufacturer identifiers. Cannot be true with a barcode or MPN. The response’s identifier_status is provided when identifiers exist, not_applicable when this flag is true, and unknown otherwise.

overall_low_stock_threshold.description: Overall low-stock threshold for directly tracked simple products. Uses total available stock across locations. Zero is valid. On update, null disables the alert and omission keeps it. Not available for untracked or group-backed stock. Simple products only.

prices.description: Simple products only. Rows are {currency_code, regular_price, sale_price?, cost_price?, sale_starts_at?, sale_ends_at?}. Amounts are JSON decimal strings with the currency’s permitted precision. Include the base currency. On update, supplying this array replaces the complete price set. A sale price may be zero but must be below the regular price. The base-currency sale schedule applies to all currency sale prices; a non-base sale requires a base sale. Omit sale prices from the replacement set to remove them.

publish_at.description: Publication time, required when the resulting status is scheduled. Accepts an ISO 8601 timestamp; include an offset for an explicit instant, or use the store timezone for a local timestamp. Stay within publish_max_days_ahead from GET /products/limits. Invalid local times during a daylight-saving change are rejected; a repeated local time uses its first occurrence. Changing to another status clears the schedule.

quantity_tiers.description: Complete quantity-pricing ladder set for this Product. Supplying the field replaces every Product and Variant ladder atomically; an empty array clears them, while omission leaves them unchanged. Each row is `{target_type, target_id, min_quantity, percent}`. `target_type` is `product` or `variant`; a Product target uses this Product's id and a Variant target must belong to this Product. `min_quantity` is inclusive. `percent` is an exact decimal string representing the percentage discount from the otherwise applicable Product or Variant price. Rows are capped by the limits returned from `GET /products/{id}/quantity-pricing`, and minimum quantities must increase within each target ladder. Example: `[{"target_type":"product","target_id":42,"min_quantity":10,"percent":"5.25"}]`.

removed_variant_ids.description: Variant ids to delete. Removing the last variant of a variable product is rejected. Removals and additions in one request are validated together, so replacing a combination in one call works.

requires_shipping.description: Defaults to true and can be changed on update. Variants follow this value unless they set their own requires_shipping. While it is false, the product and every variant that follows it reject weight, dimensions, customs fields, and per-item shipping prices; values stored earlier are kept but not used.

seo_description.description: Search-engine description. Whitespace is trimmed and control characters are rejected. See seo_description_max_length.

seo_title.description: Search-engine title. Whitespace is trimmed and control characters are rejected. See seo_title_max_length.

shipping_prices.description: Simple products only. Per-currency flat shipping overrides: {currency_code, price}. Send price as an exact decimal string using that currency's precision.

short_description.description: Plain-text summary. Surrounding whitespace is removed and control characters are rejected. See short_description_max_length.

sku.description: Required product SKU, including for a variable parent. ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, periods, and slashes are accepted. Trimmed and kept as entered, and unique across products, variants, and inventory groups in the store regardless of letter casing: ABC-1 and abc-1 are the same SKU. See sku_max_length.

slug.description: URL slug. Omit on create to generate it from the title. A source slug must use lowercase, hyphen-separated words and stay within slug_max_length. A duplicate source slug receives a suffix. On update, omit to keep it; changing it creates a redirect unless create_redirect is false.

status.description: Product status: draft, active, scheduled, or archived. Defaults to draft. Scheduled products require publish_at. Active products are available only through their assigned sales channels. Allowed values: `active`, `scheduled`, `draft`, `archived`.

tag_ids.description: Tag IDs in this store, up to max_tags. Duplicates are removed. On update, replaces the assignment set; [] clears it and omission keeps it.

tax_classes.description: Per-market tax assignment: {market_id, tax_class_id}. Supplied array replaces the full set.

template_handle.description: Existing product template handle for this store. Use default_product for the default template. Omit on update to keep the assignment; an empty string is invalid.

title.description: Product title. Required on create; cannot be empty on update. Normalized to NFC. Control characters are rejected. See title_max_length in GET /products/limits.

variants.description: Variable products only: entries address existing variants by `variant_id` and change only the supplied fields. Variants not mentioned are untouched. Supplying `attribute_values` replaces that Variant's complete combination; it must cover the Product's declared attributes and remain unique across all surviving and concurrently updated Variants. Supplying `prices` replaces the complete currency set and cannot be empty. Supplying `shipping_prices` replaces the complete set and an empty array clears it. `requires_shipping` takes `true` or `false` to set the variant's own value, or null to return it to the product's setting; omit it to leave it unchanged. When a variant stops shipping, its stored weight, dimensions, customs fields, and shipping prices are cleared, and supplying non-empty values for them is rejected. Supplying `inventory` sets only the named locations. Include `expected_quantity` in each edited location row to reject a stale stock snapshot with PRODUCT_VERSION_STALE (409). Omit unchanged locations when editing other fields. Example — reprice one variant: `{"variants": [{"variant_id": 1007, "prices": [{"currency_code": "USD", "regular_price": "31.00"}]}]}`.

weight_unit.description: Weight unit; required with weight. Allowed values: `kg`, `g`, `lb`, `oz`.

Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for PUT /api/2025-01/pages/{id}/metafields/{namespace}/{key}/translations/{locale}. Only the connected store is accessible. description: Create an operational order. Order numbers are assigned automatically. Supplying order_number or order_number_seq, including null or an empty value, returns ORDER_NUMBER_READ_ONLY (400). Use external_order_id for the source system’s identifier. Creates an order through the same pricing, tax, duty, inventory, fulfillment, audit, and webhook pipeline as Store Admin. When duty applies and an item cannot be rated (no HS code, no country of origin, no weight for a per-kg rate, no rate for its origin, or a duty rule in another currency), creation is refused with the matching `ORDER_DUTY_*` error (422) naming the product, with `details.product_id`, `details.variant_id`, `details.cause` and `details.unrated_lines` listing every such item; fix the product or the duty rule, or send `duty_override` with the duties override scope. Hosted checkout charges no duty on such items instead. `ORDER_DUTY_CALCULATION_FAILED` (502) means duty rules could not be read; nothing was created, so the same request can be retried. When tax pricing needs a recognised state, creation returns `ORDER_TAX_ZONE_NEEDS_STATE` with `details.tax_zone_needs_state: true` and `details.tax_basis_applied`; supply that state and preview again before creating a payable order. A preview with unresolved state and zero tax is not a final zero-tax quote. Inclusive exemption settles commercial rules once before removing included tax: 120 less a fixed 12 discount at 20% becomes 90, while a separately resolved 10% fee of 12 becomes 10. Exemption rounds line amounts rather than unit amounts: 100 units at 1 including 20% gives a line of 83.33. Stored line totals are authoritative, including rounding remainders. The pricing snapshot retains each item's `commercial_unit_price`, `commercial_line_total` and `commercial_discount_total`, and discounts' `commercial_amount` and allocation `commercial_total_discount`, before exemption. Edits use this commercial evidence while unchanged lines keep their settled tax and net amounts. The tax snapshot preserves `zone_needs_state` independently of `zone_unmatched`. All create requests must send `Idempotency-Key`. App tokens must also send a stable `external_order_id`. A store-admin token scopes its retry key to that user and store. Repeating the same request returns the existing order; reusing the key for different details returns 409. Sales-channel attribution is derived from the app installation. Ordinary apps and store-admin tokens create channel-less orders. Do not send channel or creator fields. checkout_id, source_cart_id and source_cart_version_id are checkout-owned and rejected here. Historical CSV imports use a separate archival workflow and do not trigger operational order webhooks, inventory, fulfillment, or customer messages. The sample request creates an unpaid custom-item order. Replace the customer ID and address with values from your store. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for POST /api/2025-01/orders. Only the connected store is accessible. Preserve omitted fields. Present confirmation impact before resubmitting with confirmation; inspect bulk success and failure results. Do not retry an uncertain write automatically.

billing_address.description: Billing address snapshot. Its country selects the market when no shipping country is present.

cod_fee_override.description: Non-negative COD fee amount in the order currency; requires the cod override scope and an eligible COD order.

coupon_codes.description: Coupon codes to evaluate through the pricing engine. A free-gift offer prices its gift at zero only when the gift is sent as an ordinary item line (product_id and, for a variant, variant_id), up to the offered quantity; extra units are charged.

currency_code.description: Requested presentment currency. It must match the resolved market for the address country.

customer_email.description: Customer email snapshot. Identity and current customer details resolve from customer_id.

customer_first_name.description: Optional first-name snapshot; the existing customer record is authoritative.

customer_id.description: Existing customer id in this store. Operational creation requires this customer; create the customer first when necessary. Customer snapshot fields resolve from this record.

customer_last_name.description: Optional last-name snapshot; the existing customer record is authoritative.

customer_note.description: Customer note stored on the order.

customer_phone.description: Optional phone snapshot; the existing customer record is authoritative.

customer_tax_exempt.description: Explicit staff approval for this order. Applies only in an enabled zone with effect=exempt and records source staff_order. Otherwise the merchant's customer tax_exempt flag supplies customer_flag. No live registration or exemption check is performed.

customer_tax_id.description: Tax ID for the resolved tax zone. Uses the shared offline format/check-digit validation and normalization. Invalid values return TAX_ID_INVALID with field customer_tax_id. Does not grant exemption. Omit to use the customer's saved ID only when its type and validation match the zone. An invalid saved ID is ignored without blocking pricing or payment.

duty_override.description: Non-negative duty amount in the order currency; requires the duties override scope. Currency precision is enforced.

excluded_discount_ids.description: Automatic discounts to omit, up to 250 identifiers. These exclusions apply when the order is priced and saved.

expected_total.description: Optional reviewed grand total in the order currency, before Store Credit or gift-card payment. Creation recalculates current prices and returns ORDER_TOTAL_CHANGED (409) if the total has changed. Review the new total before submitting a new request.

external_order_id.description: Stable source order id. Required for app tokens; omit for a store-admin token creating a manual order.

idempotency_key.description: Stable key for this exact order write. Reuse only for the same request after an uncertain response.

items.description: Order lines. product_id and variant_id are integer JSON numbers, not strings. A variable product requires an exact variant. Catalog prices and snapshots are resolved at creation; supplied prices cannot override a catalog price. For a custom line omit both IDs, provide title, quantity, unit_price, taxable and requires_shipping, and provide weight with weight_unit (g, kg, oz or lb), harmonized_code and country_of_origin when needed by shipping or duty rules. Custom unit_price is a non-negative plain decimal string, including zero, with no currency symbol, grouping or exponent. Non-zero digits beyond the currency scale return ORDER_AMOUNT_TOO_PRECISE. Each line may include manual_discount with type fixed or percentage, positive decimal-string value and optional name (100 characters). Percentage values are capped at 100 with at most two decimal places. Fixed values fit the currency scale.

locale.description: Order language, such as fr or en-GB. It must be a language the store has enabled; customer emails and the payment page use it. Defaults to the store language.

manual_discount.description: Order-level discount: type fixed or percentage, positive decimal-string value, and optional name (100 characters). Percentages allow at most 100 and two decimal places; fixed amounts use the order currency scale. Savings cannot exceed eligible merchandise.

order_confirmation.description: Order confirmation only: email and message are independent booleans, each defaulting to false. For example {"email":true,"message":false}. Null, non-boolean values and unknown keys are rejected. Choices are saved with the order and respected when payment completes. True requests sending subject to store notification settings, customer contact, template, sender/provider and allowance. Omission does not request confirmation. Other order notifications use the merchant’s independent event controls. Successful refunds distinguish partial from full repayment of captured funds. Cancellation does not move money and selects one cancellation notification based on completed refunds at cancellation; a refund completed later can notify separately. Pending or failed provider refunds do not send completed-refund notifications. Customer-facing refund amounts preserve settlement decimals in the order currency; API money remains exact decimal strings. Order history records the request and subsequent sending outcomes.

override_scopes.description: Independent boolean exceptions: discounts, limits, cod, fees and duties. When this object is present it replaces legacy admin_override behavior; omitted members are false. Overriding one scope never enables another. The discounts scope lifts the market stacking rules (single mode, coupon limit, automatic-and-code combination) up to the platform code limit, but two offers still cannot use the same item units: a bundle, buy X get Y or free-gift offer whose items are already claimed by a higher-ranked offer does not apply. COD fee overrides do not bypass destination eligibility.

payment.description: Initial payment record, not a request to charge a provider. Members: method (required; lowercase identifier such as card, upi, cash, bank_transfer or cod), status (required; pending, authorized, captured, failed, refunded or partially_refunded), provider (the gateway or channel that took the money, for example stripe or marketplace), provider_payment_id (that gateway's payment or transaction reference), currency_code (must match the order), amount, card_brand, card_last4, cash_given, cash_change, exchange_rate, processing_fee and processing_fee_currency (all decimals are plain strings). For operational creation, amount is replaced by the full authoritative order total. Use captured only when payment has actually been received. An absent payment leaves the balance unpaid. COD must be pending, and a pending COD record does not mark the order paid. A payment record cannot be combined with send_payment_link, or with store_credit_amount unless it is COD. On development and transfer stores every order is a test order and recorded payments are refused, except an app token's own checkout recording a payment that names provider (not manual) and provider_payment_id; cash on delivery is always refused there.

selected_optional_fee_ids.description: Currently available optional checkout fees to apply. Invalid or unavailable selections are rejected.

send_payment_link.description: Email the customer a link to pay this order on the store's hosted payment page, through the store's payment providers for the order's market (test providers on development and transfer stores). Requires a customer email and at least one payment provider for that market. Cannot be combined with payment.

shipping_address.description: Shipping address snapshot. Its country selects the market when present.

shipping_amount.description: Final shipping charge in currency_code. Used only when shipping_override is true.

shipping_method.description: Customer-facing shipping method name. Required when shipping_override is true.

shipping_method_id.description: A shipping option previously resolved for these lines and this address. Required for shippable lines unless an external shipping override is supplied.

shipping_override.description: Set true when the connected sales channel supplies the final shipping charge instead of selecting a store shipping option.

status_slug.description: Optional configured workflow status. New operational orders cannot start cancelled. Workflow labels do not set payment or fulfillment state.

store_credit_amount.description: Store Credit payment in the order currency. Checked against the live customer balance, order total and merchant per-order allowance, then reserved atomically. It does not reduce the taxable base. Any remaining amount remains unpaid. It cannot be combined with a non-COD payment record.

name: create_order

description: Fetch one order with fulfillment plans. Order numbers are assigned using the merchant’s numbering settings and store timezone. They are immutable identifiers, not money-formatted values. Do not assume a gapless sequence or predict the next identifier. Period resets use the configured starting number; random mode does not consume the sequential counter. Tax is split across `items[].tax_lines`, `shipping_tax_lines`, `cod_fee_tax_lines`, `duty_tax_lines` and `checkout_fee_lines[].tax_lines`; these amounts sum to `tax_total`. Refunds expose `goods_total`, `tax_total` and `components` (actual returned amount, goods_amount, tax_amount, original tax_lines and item or charge identity). Item refunds also expose goods_amount, tax_amount and tax_lines. Components include amount-only allocations; quantities of zero do not return stock. Tax is prorated from the saved tax lines over remaining units or charge amounts, with the final unit taking the remainder, capped at collected tax less active refund reservations. Smaller refund amounts reduce tax proportionally. Money above selected units and charges is allocated across the remaining order without returning additional units. A component key identifies its source and can repeat for selected-unit and additional monetary allocations. Surplus money that was never sale value has no tax. Only completed refunds reduce tax reports. Base refund goods and tax consume each item's or charge's saved base allocations cumulatively, including its final remainder. Fully refunded products have zero net goods revenue. The signed base_rounding_amount reconciles settled cash with base_goods_amount plus base_tax_amount without moving revenue or tax between products. Snapshot items carry an immutable allocation_key, preserved when imports replace database IDs; supplied sale allocations and original refund evidence are validated and retained. Historical order CSV exports preserve refunds (per-refund components and original tax_lines), line_id and base_refunded_total. Imports reject missing or inconsistent refund evidence with ORDER_IMPORT_REFUND_EVIDENCE_INVALID; they never estimate taxable refund history from refunded_total. Returns the order-time pricing, tax, fee, and duty snapshot plus owner-generated fulfillment_orders, their fixed locations and package snapshots, remaining line quantities, and actual fulfillments. `customer_tax_id` and `customer_tax_id_type` record the normalized, offline-validated ID and never prove registration or exemption. `tax_exemption_source` is customer_flag, staff_order or none, and `tax_id_state_mismatch` flags a GSTIN whose state differs from the Indian tax address. Saved customer IDs are used only when their type and validation match the zone; invalid saved IDs are ignored without blocking pricing or payment; `tax_exempt` and `invoice_only` are server-computed outcomes. `is_tax_included` records whether the order's prices include tax, and `tax_basis_applied` which address taxed it (`shipping` or `billing`). Each item's `tax_lines` list its taxes with `name`, `rate`, `amount`, `base_amount` (the amount in the store's base currency), `jurisdiction` (the ISO 3166-2 subdivision of the matched state zone, such as `IN-UP`, otherwise the tax country, such as `IN`) and `jurisdiction_type` (`subdivision` or `country`). Inclusive checkout shows VAT on duty as a separate added amount: 120 goods + 12 duty + 2.40 duty VAT = 134.40, with only 20 goods VAT labelled included. The item's `tax_rate` is the sum of its tax lines' rates (CGST 9% + SGST 9% is 18), on create and edit alike. Tax is calculated at full precision on discounted amounts across the order; `tax_total` is rounded once to currency precision (half to even), then allocated across item lines, shipping, COD, duty tax and checkout fees by largest remainder, so line amounts always add up. Cart and checkout use each line's allocated tax for display. Thus 100 separate exclusive 0.25 lines at 19% have 4.75 tax: 75 lines receive 0.05 and 25 receive 0.04, displaying 75 times 0.30 plus 25 times 0.29 = 29.75, exactly the amount charged, with zero savings. A single 100-unit line also has 4.75 tax and 29.75 payable. When a merchant-approved tax-exempt buyer orders in a tax-inclusive market, every amount is charged without its included tax: `tax_exempt` is `true`, `is_tax_included` stays `true` and `tax_total` is 0. An item's `duty_customs_value` is its value after discounts without the tax its price includes, plus its share of shipping (when the country rule includes shipping) and of checkout fees that count toward customs value. When duty is collected at checkout, the import VAT on it is part of `tax_total` and listed in `pricing_snapshot.tax.duty_tax_lines`. `duty_collection_mode` records who pays import duties on an international shipment and is empty for domestic orders. When it is `collect_at_checkout`, `duty_total` is collected and included in `grand_total`. When it is `pay_on_delivery`, `duty_total` plus `duty_tax_estimate` is the customer's estimate, outside `grand_total`. When it is `included_in_price`, they are the merchant's estimated duty cost, outside `grand_total` and not revenue. Estimates come from the merchant's rules; carriers and customs may charge differently. Apps must fulfill beneath one open plan and cannot choose another location. Item properties are order-time snapshots of cart-line values, filtered by the token’s access to each definition. Declaring an order-item metafield with the same key does not copy an ordinary property into it. Artifact IDs do not grant access to private files. `version` starts at 1 and increases by one every time the merchant or an app edits the order's items; send it as order_version with writes that depend on the order's contents. Each entry in `discounts` lists its `allocations`: the part of that discount that reduced each order item (`order_item_id`, the `quantity` of units it reduced, `amount`, and `is_free` when it made those units free). A discount's allocations sum to its amount and an item's allocations sum to its `discount_amount`; an order-level manual discount is split in proportion to what each item has left after the other discounts. Quantity edits preserve discount shares consumed or reserved by refunds and prorate only the remaining aggregate discount over the remaining units; the saved allocations and pricing totals reconcile to those shares. Orders saved without pricing evidence have none. Each refund item reports `amount`, the refunded units at the item's unit price less their share of its discounts, and `discount_allocations`, each discount's share: the remaining aggregate line discount is prorated over the remaining units and rounded once, then distributed between discounts with each share capped at its remaining allocation. Successful and pending refunds consume shares; failed provider refunds release them. The final available units receive the unconsumed discount. Item amounts always subtract the authoritative line discount, even if historical per-discount allocations are unavailable. Historical refund breakdowns are reconstructed deterministically from the saved line allocations. The refund's own amount is what was returned and can differ from its items. An item that does not require shipping has no fulfillment: its `fulfillment_status` becomes `fulfilled` and `fulfilled_quantity` equals its quantity when captured payments cover the order total plus any returned surplus and the order is not cancelled. Refund status alone never fulfills a line. The order's `fulfillment_status` counts every item, so an unpaid order of only such items is `unfulfilled`. A pickup order carries `pickup_location`: the store location the customer collects it from, as chosen at checkout (`id`, `name`, address fields, `phone`, `ready_in`, `instructions`, `hours`); it is null for a delivery order. A pickup order's fulfillments move `pending` → `ready_for_pickup` → `picked_up` (or `cancelled`), with `ready_for_pickup_at` and `picked_up_at`; `picked_up` counts as delivered. A delivery order never takes a pickup status, and a pickup order never a delivery one. `checkout_answers` lists the shopper's answers to the store's checkout question, frozen when the order was placed: `block_id`, `kind` (`text` or `checkbox`), `label` (the question in the store's default language), `value` (what the shopper entered, `yes` for a ticked checkbox) and `locale` (the shopper's checkout language); it is empty when checkout asked nothing. Nobody can change answers after the order exists. Each entry in `payments` carries `label`, the payment method's name in the request language: a payment app's payment is named by the app that collected it, the platform's own methods by their name (for example Gift card or Cash on Delivery), and any other recorded method reads Other payment method. Show `label`; `method` stays the recorded identifier. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for GET /api/2025-01/orders/{id}. Only the connected store is accessible.

description: See what an edit would do, without changing anything. Computes an edit exactly as applying it would: the new totals, the balance the customer would owe or the refund due, the refund methods available, each line's change and the fulfillment orders and apps it would affect. Nothing is saved, reserved or sent, and no Idempotency-Key is needed. Changes eligible items, prices, manual discounts, contact, addresses and shipping of a placed order through the same edit Store Admin uses, with the same rules: lines can be lowered or removed down to what has shipped, been refunded or is being refunded; products, variants and custom items can be added; gift-card lines cannot change. Added products are priced at the current price in the order's market, or with price_basis original at the price already on the order for the same product. Prices, manual discounts and delivery changes require fulfillment and item refunds not to have started. Contact corrections never change the customer account. The order keeps its currency and original exchange rate. While the normalised country and state of the effective tax address recorded by tax_basis_applied are unchanged, items whose quantity, unit price and discounts are unchanged keep the tax lines and rates they were sold with, and so do the COD fee and checkout fees; only changed or new items and shipping are taxed again at current rates. Changes to the unused address or equivalent state spellings preserve pins: changing billing alone under shipping basis keeps 700 tax on 100 unchanged 100 lines sold at 7%, even if current rates are 8%. If the effective tax address changes, everything is taxed again. Amounts a tax-exempt buyer in a tax-inclusive market already pays without tax, including freshly priced additions and carried fees, are not reduced again. Omitting updates.shipping.amount carries its stored net amount; an explicitly supplied amount or newly selected quote uses the inclusive entry basis, regardless of spelling or equality to the saved amount. At 20%, carried shipping of 12 stays 12, while supplying 12.00 or 12.0000 both settles to 10. Commercial discounts and fees settle once before exemption: 120 including 20% less a fixed 12 discount becomes 90. Exemption rounds the whole line, so 100 units at 1 including 20% becomes 83.33; stored line totals, not rounded unit prices multiplied by quantity, remain authoritative. Repricing preserves the historical tax ID and type without validating them against current zone rules or importing the customer’s current saved ID. Current customer approval and the current zone’s effect determine exemption for recalculated amounts; staff approval comes only from staff_order provenance. Unchanged exempt lines retain their sold net amounts even after approval changes, and retained taxable lines or fees prevent whole-order exemption. Applied exemption source and GSTIN state mismatch reconcile atomically with totals. Repricing preserves unrelated fees and keeps existing promotions on their original target items, capped at their edited value. Orders with duties, cancelled or imported orders, orders with an authorized but uncaptured payment, and orders placed before editing existed cannot be edited. order_version must be the order's current version; any other value is refused so an edit never overwrites a change you have not seen. Every successful edit raises the version by one, is recorded on the order timeline and audit log under your app's name, and sends orders/edited with edited_by_app_id set to your app. Apps that had already received a changed fulfillment order must acknowledge it by writing with the new version. phone_country_code.description: Two-letter country/region hint for a national phone number, such as KR; not a calling code such as +82. An international number determines its own region. See [Phone numbers and country codes](/store-api/reference/phone-numbers).

Format/check-digit checks are offline and do not verify registration. Custom customer IDs are free text. Checkout uses a saved ID only if it passes the matched zone's optional pattern and type rules; an invalid saved ID is ignored without blocking pricing or payment.

description: List the store's enabled languages with the default flagged. Returns every enabled language with `locale`, `label` (English), `native_name`, `selector_label`, `rtl`, `is_default`, and `created_at` (RFC 3339 in the store time zone). Selector labels use the native name followed by the English name in parentheses when they differ. This read returns `success` and `data`, without success `code` or `message`. The response also includes the store's language limit, `max_languages`, which counts distinct enabled languages, including the default language, and is never below 1. Once a downgrade is scheduled, it is the lower plan's limit. Locale codes use their canonical spelling, for example `pt-BR`. Content is authored in the default language and translated into the others. This list is the catalog a storefront can publish. Assigning those languages to a specific storefront is an Online Store Admin action and is not part of this resource. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for GET /api/2025-01/languages. Only the connected store is accessible.
name: list_languages

description: Update the store's enabled language set. When `locales` is supplied, it is the complete set of locale codes the store should publish in. Repeated codes count once, and an identical set is a no-op that does not claim an update. Omitting `locales` or sending `null` returns the current list without changes. An unchanged set returns HTTP 200 with `success` and `data`, without `code` or `message`. Whitespace is trimmed, blank entries are ignored, and an empty resulting set is rejected. The default language must always be included in a supplied set — it cannot be removed here. Disabling a language permanently deletes its translations and requires confirmation: the first call that would remove locales returns `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` with warnings and a token bound to those locales; repeat with `confirmed: true` and that token. Adding languages does not require confirmation. Locale codes are matched without regard to letter case and stored in their canonical spelling, for example `pt-BR`. A language that is assigned to a storefront is protected (remove it from those storefronts first). The set size is capped by `max_languages`; once a downgrade is scheduled, the lower plan's limit applies. A store above the limit can keep or shrink its set. A replacement that adds any language must finish at or below the limit, even if it removes other languages at the same time. Disabling a language cancels its active translation work and publishes `store/locales/deleted` for each removed language, in addition to `store/locales/update`. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for PUT /api/2025-01/languages. Only the connected store is accessible. Preserve omitted fields. description: List the store's currencies with their settings. Returns the store's complete currency set, including the base currency and any added currencies. Each currency includes its conversion rate, `rate_source`, rounding mode, the rounding modes it can use, enabled state, and timestamps. The base currency keeps its original prices and cannot be rounded, so its `rounding_modes` is always empty. `conversion_rate` converts base to currency: `amount_in_currency = amount_in_base * conversion_rate`. This is the direction of exchange-rate `rate_inverse`, the opposite of exchange-rate `rate`. It is the rate prices use right now: in manual mode it is the merchant's stored rate (`rate_source: "manual"`); in automatic-rate mode it is the live market cross-rate from the current exchange-rate snapshot (`rate_source: "automatic"`), and when no current snapshot exists it is empty with `rate_source: "automatic_unavailable"`—prices in that currency cannot be charged until rates refresh. Exchange rates always use `.` as the decimal separator. Use conversion_rate from currency reads for the effective rate, never the rounded reference table. Names and rate_message are backend-localized; show rate_message verbatim. Use All exchange rates only for reference. Live rate refreshes do not fire `currencies/update`; re-read currencies when you need the current automatic rate. The response also shows whether multi-currency is enabled and available on the store's plan, whether rates are automatic, every rounding mode the platform supports, and the store's currency limits. The top-level `rounding_modes` includes `nearest_99`, `nearest_95` and `nearest_50`, which zero-decimal currencies such as JPY reject; offer each currency its own `rounding_modes` instead. `max_conversion_decimals` is the service constant (10); `max_conversion_rate`, `max_per_store` (including the base currency), and `bulk_max` come from the service configuration keys `CURRENCY_MAX_CONVERSION_RATE`, `CURRENCY_MAX_PER_STORE`, and `CURRENCY_BULK_MAX`. Example values are illustrative; read the response to validate manual rates and limits. `bulk_max` caps currency batches, including the bulk data-removal endpoint. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for GET /api/2025-01/currencies. Only the connected store is accessible.

This is the direction of exchange-rate `rate_inverse`, the opposite of exchange-rate `rate`. It is the rate prices use right now: in manual mode it is the merchant's stored rate (`rate_source: "manual"`); in automatic-rate mode it is the live market cross-rate from the current exchange-rate snapshot (`rate_source: "automatic"`), and when no current snapshot exists it is empty with `rate_source: "automatic_unavailable"`—prices in that currency cannot be charged until rates refresh. Exchange rates always use `.` as the decimal separator. Use conversion_rate from currency reads for the effective rate, never the rounded reference table. Names and rate_message are backend-localized; show rate_message verbatim. Use All exchange rates only for reference. Live rate refreshes do not fire `currencies/update`; re-read currencies when you need the current automatic rate. Market assignment still determines which currencies a shopper may use. Use the resolved active market—not this store-wide list alone—to build a shopper-facing currency selector. description: Current market rates for supported currencies, relative to the store's base. Returns current market rates for supported currencies relative to the store's base currency. Each entry carries `base_currency` and the rate in both directions as decimal strings: `rate` is the currency-to-base multiplier (`amount_in_base = amount_in_currency * rate`), while `rate_inverse` is the base-to-currency multiplier (`amount_in_currency = amount_in_base * rate_inverse`). The request fails with HTTP 503 when no complete, unexpired snapshot is available. The store's base currency is not included in `rates`. description: Create a market for one or more countries. Provide a name and at least one country. Every store starts with a primary market, created with the store and named after its base currency, that serves every country. Each country can belong to only one market. Countries another market serves move to the new market: the first request returns `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, whose warnings name each country and the market it leaves; repeat it with `confirmed: true` and the `confirmation_token` to create the market and move them in one transaction, so they are never left without a market. A market that would be left with no countries refuses the move with `MARKET_COUNTRY_MOVE_EMPTIES_MARKET`, and a country still used by one of its tax, shipping, or cash-on-delivery zones cannot leave it. You may provide a URL-safe slug or let Tringify generate one from the name, adding `-2`, `-3` and so on when that slug is taken. New markets begin with the store's base currency. They are active by default, calculate tax from the shipping address using tax-exclusive catalog prices, use the default tax class, and leave duties disabled. A successful request returns the created market and publishes `markets/create`. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for POST /api/2025-01/markets. Only the connected store is accessible. Present confirmation impact before resubmitting with confirmation; inspect bulk success and failure results. Do not retry an uncertain write automatically.

confirmation_token.description: Token returned with `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` when the new market takes countries from other markets.

confirmed.description: Set to `true`, with `confirmation_token`, to repeat a create that returned `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` because it moves countries from other markets.

countries.description: Uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes for the countries served by this market. Repeated codes are ignored. Each country can belong to only one market; countries another market serves move here after confirmation.

currency_code.description: Store base currency. You may omit this field because every new market starts with the base currency.

name.description: Name of the market. Names are unique within a store and are matched without regard to letter case.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier. When omitted, Tringify generates it from the market name.

description: Retrieve a market by id. Returns the market's settings, countries, and assigned currencies. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for GET /api/2025-01/markets/{marketId}. Only the connected store is accessible.
name: get_market

description: Change a market's settings. Send only the fields you want to change. To avoid overwriting someone else's change, send the `revision` you last read as `expected_revision`: if the market changed since, the request fails with `MARKET_CHANGED` and nothing is saved. When provided, `countries` and `currency_codes` replace their complete existing lists. Always retain the store's base currency in `currency_codes`; other currencies require a store plan with multi-currency support. Every market country has a serving currency, and newly added countries initially use the store's base currency. Countries another market serves move to this one: the request asks for confirmation naming each country and the market it leaves, then moves them in the same transaction. A market left with no countries refuses with `MARKET_COUNTRY_MOVE_EMPTIES_MARKET`. A country cannot be removed while a tax, shipping, or cash-on-delivery zone still uses it, and a currency cannot be removed while a country or duty rule uses it. Removing a currency also removes its exact shipping overrides; adding it back later converts blank shipping values from the base again. A single update can add or remove at most the market-currency bulk limit. While the market has price-based tax rules, replacing its currency is refused with `TAX_PRICE_RULE_BLOCKS_CURRENCY_CHANGE`, because rule thresholds are amounts in the current currency. `tax_included` controls whether catalog prices already contain tax, while `tax_display_mode` controls how storefront prices are presented. Tax is calculated on the order total, rounded once and allocated across lines by largest remainder, so line amounts always add up. Cart and checkout display each line using its allocated tax and represent mixed-display discounts as signed differences. For 100 separate exclusive 0.25 lines at 19%, tax is 4.75 and both display and charge total 29.75, with zero savings. Inclusive 1100 discounted to 1045 across a 1000 threshold at 5%/12% displays exclusive 982.14 minus a signed discount of -13.10 = 995.24, plus 49.76 tax = 1045. A negative displayed discount is a tax adjustment, not additional savings; render it as an increase instead of hiding or clamping it. Moving countries from other markets, changing `tax_included`, and deactivating a market with unpaid checkout orders first return `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` with `details.warnings` and `details.confirmation_token`; repeat the request with `confirmed: true` and that `confirmation_token` to proceed. Confirmation is checked against the current market row under its transaction lock; a concurrent change cannot bypass it, even without expected_revision. Changing `tax_included` always asks: every price keeps its number, so the warning (`MARKET_TAX_INCLUDED_ON_WARNING` or `MARKET_TAX_INCLUDED_OFF_WARNING`) explains that a price of 100 then means 100 with tax included, or 100 before tax. Deactivating a market asks when checkout orders in it are still waiting for payment. A request that does several returns one set of warnings, and one token confirms it. Successful changes return the updated market and publish `markets/update`. Sending only values that are already saved changes nothing and publishes no event, unless a market country was missing its serving currency, in which case that country is given the base currency. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for PATCH /api/2025-01/markets/{marketId}. Only the connected store is accessible. Present confirmation impact before resubmitting with confirmation; inspect bulk success and failure results. Do not retry an uncertain write automatically.

confirmation_token.description: Token returned with `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` when moving countries from other markets, changing `tax_included`, or deactivating a market that has checkout orders waiting for payment. One token covers everything the request asks for.

confirmed.description: Set to `true`, with `confirmation_token`, to repeat a country move, `tax_included` change or deactivation that returned `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`.

countries.description: Complete list of uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes the market should serve. Countries omitted from this list are removed; repeated codes are ignored.

currency_codes.description: Complete list of currencies assigned to the market. Always include the store's base currency. A single update can add or remove at most the market-currency bulk limit.

duties_enabled.description: Estimate duties with country rules: whether the market's enabled duty rules price an estimate for international shipments. Estimates come from your own rules; carriers and customs may charge a different amount, including their own handling fees. Turning this off with `duty_collection_mode` `collect_at_checkout` fails with `MARKET_DUTY_COLLECT_NEEDS_ESTIMATES`.

duty_collection_mode.description: Who pays import duties on international shipments (an item's country of origin differs from the destination). `pay_on_delivery`: the customer pays on delivery; checkout, order pages and emails say import duties and taxes may be due on delivery, with the estimate, when a rule prices one, shown below the total and never added to it. `collect_at_checkout`: the customer pays at checkout; the estimated duty and the import tax on it (at each item's tax rates) are added to the total, and shoppers are told nothing is due on delivery. Requires `duties_enabled`. `included_in_price`: you pay, and your prices already cover it; nothing is added to the total, shoppers are told duties and taxes are included, and an estimate a rule prices is recorded on the order as your estimated duty cost. The statement shows whether or not estimates are on; domestic orders show none. You are responsible for this choice.

expected_revision.description: The market `revision` you last read. When provided and the market has changed since, the request fails with `MARKET_CHANGED`.

is_active.description: Whether the market can serve customers. The primary market must remain active.

name.description: Name of the market. Names are unique within a store and are matched without regard to letter case.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier for the market.

tax_basis.description: Address used to calculate tax: `shipping` or `billing`. Orders without shippable items use the billing address.

tax_display_mode.description: Whether storefront prices are displayed with tax included (`inclusive`) or excluded (`exclusive`).

tax_enabled.description: Whether tax is calculated for orders in this market.

tax_included.description: Whether catalog prices already include tax. Changing it requires confirmation: prices keep their numbers, so each price changes what it charges.

description: Read availability and currency coverage of connected providers. Connect providers in store settings first. This endpoint returns market enablement, ordering, readiness and supported currencies without provider credentials. A provider appears here once a payment app is installed on the store: installing it creates a binding (`binding_id`) in `pending_configuration`, listed in every market with `status` `setup_required`. The merchant then connects their account inside the app, and the app reports it through `POST /service-bindings/{id}/configuration-changed`. Tringify asks the app to attest the connection (mode, account country, operations, presentment currencies); a successful attestation makes the binding `ready`. A ready provider is `eligible` in a market when it supports at least one of the market's currencies (otherwise `currency_unavailable`). Enable it per market with Update market payment provider; enabled, ready providers are offered at checkout in `sort_order`. On development and transfer stores only test-mode connections can be enabled, and the platform test gateway is enabled in the primary market the first time it attests. `status` is `setup_required`, `currency_unavailable` (the provider supports none of the market's currencies), `ready` or `active`; `eligible` says whether it can be enabled; `currency_coverage` is `none`, `partial` or `full`, with the market currencies it does and does not support listed. Enabled providers come first, ordered by `sort_order`; the rest follow by app name. Uses the documented Store API fields, validation and permissions for GET /api/2025-01/markets/{marketId}/payment-providers. Only the connected store is accessible.
